create.name: The Astana (Inayatiyya)
create.bio:
The Astana serves as the headquarters for the Inayatiyya across North America and Oceania. It occupies a red-brick townhouse with a walled garden courtyard on East Cary Street in Richmond, Virginia. The Inayatiyya is the Sufi order founded on the teachings of Hazrat Inayat Khan, the Indian musician and mystic who brought his message of love, harmony and beauty to the West in 1910, and the Astana is where its current head, Pir Zia Inayat Khan, lives and teaches.

The name means a threshold, a word used in India for a place where Sufis gather to study and keep company, and that is the spirit of the house. Pir Zia gives classes there on chosen evenings along with occasional trainings and special programmes, while the order's wider calendar of online courses, meditation series and the two-year Suluk Academy is open to students anywhere in the world. Its teaching draws on meditation, the remembrance practice of zikr, breath, silence, music and the contemplation of nature, and on Universal Worship, a service honouring the scriptures of many faiths. Visitors who wish to come outside scheduled programmes are asked to arrange it with the house in advance.

Teachers file is empty: Pir Zia Inayat Khan, named as the Astana's primary teacher, is not on Spiritpedia (worth a teacher lead).
